messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breaches detected for dedicated-pool 'hotshot-us-west' across multiple customers. Auto-escalation: page eng-sre. Root cause suspected: autoscaler warmup delay / pool saturation. Queue depth spiking.
sarah (oncall): seeing p95 ~800ms, p99 ~3.2s for streaming responses. Streaming stalls reported. Queue depth jumped from 20 -> 230 in 3m.
matt (eng-sre): confirmed. Metrics: pool utilization 98%, cold slots 0, warmup in-flight 6, handshake failures increased. autoscaler logs show warmup latency ~90s per slot.
jess (eng-runtime): logs from worker nodes show KV cache misses at burst head, lots of cold LRU thrash. Streaming workers hitting dequeue timeout at 25s. Sample log: ```[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] queue_depth=214 processed=12 p99=3200ms warmup_pending=6" warmup_latency=90s```
pranay (eng-platform): autoscaler trace: handshake handshake_ack delayed due to node-init GC on provisioned image. Provider reported slow attach. This is consistent with recent provider-side region slowness.
eli (support): we have 3 customers flagged: Acme, Waveform, and Ledgerly reporting degraded streaming in prod. Acme reports timeouts in chat sessions. CS is aware.
nora (customer-success): onhold messages sent to Acme and Ledgerly with ETA ~30-45m, offering to failover traffic to hosted variant if customer approves.
sarah (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily route new requests to fallback 'hotshot-small' variant (lower throughput but reduces handshake), 2) manually spin extra pre-warmed pool with smaller image, 3) throttle non-critical customers by rate-limit. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
matt (eng-sre): do (2) and (1) in parallel. I'll kick manual prewarm with smaller image and force a fast boot config. Command: ```redwoodctl pools create --name hotshot-ephemeral-1 --size 8 --instance-type g4dn.xlarge --prewarm true --image fast-boot-v2```
jess (eng-runtime): on routing, we need to ensure streaming protocol compatibility for fallback. I can patch router rule to send 20% new traffic to hotshot-small for users on trial and 100% for flagged customers. Patch: ```routes.update("/v1/generate", {fallback_pool: "hotshot-small", split: {flagged:100, default:20}})```
pranay (eng-platform): kicked off manual pool create now. Provider console shows instances provisioning; ETA ~70s for attach, hoping prewarm cuts it to ~25s. Also applying overlay to reduce image init hooks.
sarah (oncall): matt, any chance to temporarily lower batch sizes to reduce tail lat? Could hit throughput but might reduce p99.
matt (eng-sre): yes, runtime config change: batch.max_tokens_per_call=512 -> 256, batch.max_wait_ms=5 -> 2. Applying now. This should reduce queuing time.
jess (eng-runtime): applied batch change. Observability: starting to see p95 drop to ~520ms within 45s. p99 still elevated while new pools join.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Action logged: manual_pool_provision started by pranay at 1755560120. Route patch applied by jess at 1755560184. Batch config updated by matt at 1755560200.
eli (support): Customer update sent to Acme: "We detected elevated latency affecting streaming. We have mitigations in progress (route fallback + spin-up). We'll follow up when p99 is under SLO or at 30m." Acme acknowledged and accepted fallback to hosted variant.
nora (customer-success): Ledgerly wants logs and timeline; prepping postmortem template.
sarah (oncall): new pool hotshot-ephemeral-1 is healthy and joined at 1755560320. Warmup complete. Observing queue drain.
matt (eng-sre): after pool join, queue depth down from 214 -> 28 in ~2m. p99 down to ~900ms, p95 stable ~480ms. Streaming stalls reduced.
jess (eng-runtime): still seeing intermittent stalls tied to a tiny subset of long-context requests that exceed KV cache window; recommending temporary prefix caching for flagged customers. Adding a per-customer cache policy for Acme and Ledgerly.
pranay (eng-platform): provider reported attach spikes in region; opened support ticket with provider to follow up on attach latency trend. Ticket ID: PROVIDER-78912.
sarah (oncall): routing split kept for flagged customers; lowering default fallback to 0% once warm pools stable.
matt (eng-sre): will keep autoscaler scaling policy under review — current plan: reduce required warmup by promoting smaller prewarm images, and add conservative headroom of +15% capacity for expected burst windows. Filing config change PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/458
eli (support): support notes: impacted customers: Acme (timeout rate peaked 11%), Waveform (errorful streams ~7%), Ledgerly (degraded latency but no timeouts). Tickets created: ACME-221, WAVE-89, LEDG-14.
nora (customer-success): postmortem owner assigned to matt. CS to coordinate customer remediation credits if needed.
sarah (oncall): handing off to matt for next 3hr on-call window. If anything re-escalates ping here and page eng-sre. :pager:
matt (eng-sre): taking the handoff. Current state: p99 trending down to ~600-900ms, pools stable, provider ticket open. Will keep rollback plan ready to reduce routing to hosted if symptoms recur.
incident-bot: :checkered_flag: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations completed (manual pools + routing + batch tuning). Monitoring for 60m. Logged severity: Sev3.
jess (eng-runtime): follow-ups: (a) add circuit-breaker to router to auto-failover flagged customers when handshake latency > 40s, (b) add KV cache telemetry for tail analysis.
pranay (eng-platform): will schedule autoscaler change in next sprint and add a canary for fast-boot images.
matt (eng-sre): postmortem draft will include timeline, root cause (provider attach & image init warmup), mitigations, and action items. ETA for draft: EOD today.
sarah (oncall): thanks team. closing on-call handoff. Keep channel open for any regressions. :white_check_mark:
